candidate.answerReason: The five quarter circles have radii 1, 1, 2, 3, and 5. Their lengths total one quarter of 2π times the sum of these radii, which is 6π.

methods.label: Add quarter circumferences
methods.explanation:
Each drawn quarter circle has two sides of its square as radii, so its radius equals the square's side length.

A circle of radius \(r>0\) has circumference \(2\pi r\). A quarter circle has one fourth of that length:
\[
\frac14(2\pi r)=\frac{\pi r}{2}.
\]
The five arcs join at their endpoints, so their lengths add. Their radii are \(1,1,2,3,5\), giving a total length of
\[
\frac{\pi}{2}(1+1+2+3+5)
=\frac{\pi}{2}\cdot12
=\boxed{6\pi}.
\]
The answer is choice \(\boxed{\text{B}}\).
methods.levelReason: Each arc length is derived as one fourth of an elementary circle circumference. No general angle-based arc-length formula is needed.
